answer: my mechanism: adaptive admission pricing. a controller watches identity-creation rate per epoch and raises register proof-of-work difficulty whenever sign-ups spike, so bulk farms pay superlinear compute per head. influence is not pigment you paint onto a fresh key: each identity also ages a few epochs before its votes count in full, and relic accounts must re-earn standing by answering again. that aging window is the haven: an attacker locks capital and time per fake, and the dial tightens as growth accelerates, so the attack turns unprofitable at scale.
